- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:518-567 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When `mktemp` fails, `|| true` leaves `_trim_count_file` empty. The Python trim still emits the UTF-8-trimmed bytes but writes no count, so `_shown_bytes` falls back to `_effective_cap`.
  WHY: The `[... TRUNCATED ...]` marker overstates the bytes shown and the prompt budget is overcharged by 1-3 bytes per truncated embed, so later inputs can be dropped early. All four reviewers rated this NIT, mapped here to low. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 reviewed the same case and did not adopt it, because the comment at lines 515-517 documents it as the intended fail-open.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:518-559 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `mktemp ... 2>/dev/null || true` swallows the mktemp failure without recording it. Only the python-failure branch keeps the documented fail-open (plain byte cut); the mktemp-failure path is neither fail-open nor fail-closed.
  WHY: Nothing is logged when the temp-file mechanism is unavailable, so an operator cannot trace a budget overcount. Both reviewers rated this NIT, mapped here to low.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:1391 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new `tests/test_prompt_invalid_utf8.py \` entry in the merge-train background pytest list duplicates the existing run at line 2922 (`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_prompt_invalid_utf8.py`), so every CI run executes the module twice.
  WHY: The duplicate adds runner time, including subprocess calls with 60s timeouts, and no coverage, because `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` is already satisfied by line 2922 (§26 runner-concurrency guidance). All reviewers rated this NIT, mapped here to low.

  PROBLEM: If `mktemp` fails to create the count file, the Python process writes no byte count and `_shown_bytes` falls back to `_effective_cap`.

  PROBLEM: `mktemp` is followed by `|| true`, which swallows possible filesystem errors.
  WHY: If directory permissions stop `mktemp`, the script silently continues with an empty `_trim_count_file` and the truncation budget calculation becomes inaccurate.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:lines 518–563 (the new mktemp-tempfile + python trim block) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/_embed_trim_count.XXXXXX"` fails, `_trim_count_file` is empty and Python emits the trimmed bytes but skips the `if count_path:` write. The check at line 558 then forces `_shown_bytes="${_effective_cap}"`, so the marker at line 561 says "first <cap> bytes shown above", and `_emit_bytes` at line 563 overcharges the budget at line 567.
  WHY: The fallback overcounts the prompt budget on every truncated file and the marker misrepresents what was emitted. Suggested fix: fall back to `head -c "${_effective_cap}" "${_p}"` when `_trim_count_file` is empty, matching the python-failure branch at lines 552–554.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:line 518 (`_trim_count_file="$(mktemp ... 2>/dev/null || true)"`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Only the python-failure branch honours the documented fail-open contract. The mktemp-failure branch silently reports the cap as the byte count, which is neither fail-open nor fail-closed, and logs nothing.
  WHY: An operator debugging a budget overcount cannot tell that the temp-file mechanism failed.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:line 1391 (new `tests/test_prompt_invalid_utf8.py \` line in the merge-train "rest" background group, lines 1387–1400) versus line 2922 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The same module is wired twice, via `pytest -q` at line 1389 and via `python3` at line 2922. Its 60s-timeout subprocess tests therefore run twice, and `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` is already satisfied by line 2922.
  WHY: Doubles the wall-clock cost of the slowest tests on every PR push and merge-train run (runner-concurrency guidance). Fix: remove line 1391.
- HARDENING: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:lines 518 and 547–554 | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=2
  PROBLEM: When `mktemp` fails, the embedder silently overcounts and misreports the marker.
  WHY: Suggested fix: branch on `[ -z "${_trim_count_file}" ]` and fall back to `head -c "${_effective_cap}" "${_p}"` with `_shown_bytes="${_effective_cap}"` (about 6 lines).
- HARDENING: .github/workflows/ci.yml:line 1391 | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: This line duplicates the wiring at line 2922.
  WHY: Suggested fix: remove the line and adjust the trailing `\` (2 lines).
